2025-14687
38 CFR Part 17
Administrative Practices and Procedures; Claims; Health Care; Health Facilities; Health Professions; Health Records; Medical Devices; Medical Research; Mental Health Programs; Veterans

Abortion bans deny women and girls our fundamental human right to comprehensive healthcare including sexual and reproductive health. Bans lead to violations of women’s rights to privacy, bodily integrity and autonomy, freedom of expression, freedom of thought, conscience, religion or belief, equality and non-discrimination, and freedom from torture and cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment and gender-based violence.

Bans ignore medical diagnoses and exclude health-threatening conditions.  Women and girls in disadvantaged situations are disproportionately affected by these bans. (Women and girls from marginalized communities, racial and ethnic minorities, migrants, women and girls with disabilities, or living on low incomes, in abusive relationships or in rural areas.)

Healthcare workers face legal consequences for their care decisions, including those regarding medically necessary or life-saving abortions or the removal of fetal tissue from women with incomplete miscarriages.
Abortion healthcare providers receive threats and are injured by crazy zealots. Bans and criminalization for providers and pregnant women, keep women and girls from engaging with the health system and seeking prenatal care. Some clinics stop providing abortion-related services, even where it remains legal. Abortion bans cause erosion of the right to privacy, as law enforcement officials increasingly rely on electronic data to track those seeking abortions or those who aid and abet them. This data can be accessed without a warrant in many cases. 

Last September, ProPublica connected the deaths of at least two women, Amber Thurman and Candi Miller, to theirs and their doctors’ confusion about what medical care was legal under Georgia’s six-week ban. A few weeks later, the nonprofit news outlet reported that two Texas women, Josseli Barnica and Nevaeh Crain, also died after doctors delayed miscarriage care. One study found that the number of women who died in Texas while pregnant, during labor, or shortly after giving birth surged by almost 60 percent after the state’s strict abortion ban went into effect. 
The fake religious based anti-abortion movement is a big lie.  It is all about denying American women control over our healthcare and our bodies.  The very same people who are behind fake religious based anti-abortion movement are also behind denying children food, housing, and medical care. 
The following link clearly blows the fake religious based anti-abortion movement wide open.
https://substack.com/home/post/p-162559653

I demand that the US government enact positive laws and regulations that ensure access to safe and legal abortion for those in the military and those not.
Health care is a right. It is not a privilege. Religious beliefs or radical right-wing ideology has no place in female healthcare. There is no such equivalent in male healthcare.

https://www.propublica.org/article/candi-miller-abortion-ban-death-georgia
